title: Hilbert's 17th: Robinson's Polynomial Is Not a Sum of Squares of Polynomials
description: Robinson's polynomial R = x⁶ + y⁶ + z⁶ − x⁴y² − y⁴z² − z⁴x² − x²y⁴ − y²z⁴ − z²x⁴ + 3x²y²z² (Robinson, 1973) is nonnegative on all of ℝ³ (its Schur-inequality certificate lives in the parent entry hilbert-17) yet — like the Motzkin polynomial — is NOT a sum of squares of polynomials. The parent entry carried this fact as the axiom robinson_not_sos_aux; this entry supplies a fully elementary, 0-axiom proof, discharging that axiom and reducing the parent's axiom count from 4 to 3. The proof is a zero-set / linear-algebra argument. Suppose R = Σᵢ qᵢ². (1) Degree bound: the degree-2D homogeneous component of a sum of squares is Σ (top form)², which over ℝ vanishes only if every top form does; since R has total degree 6, every qᵢ has total degree ≤ 3. (2) Homogeneous reduction: taking the degree-6 homogeneous component of both sides (R is homogeneous of degree 6) gives R = Σᵢ (qᵢ⁽³⁾)² with each qᵢ⁽³⁾ = homogeneousComponent 3 qᵢ a homogeneous cubic form — no bottom-degree cascade is needed. (3) Vanishing on the zero set: R vanishes at its ten real projective zeros (1,±1,0), (1,0,±1), (0,1,±1), (1,±1,±1); since a sum of real squares is 0 only if each term is, every cubic form qᵢ⁽³⁾ vanishes at all ten points. (4) The decisive linear algebra: the 10×10 matrix of the ten cubic monomials evaluated at the ten points has determinant 128 ≠ 0, so the only homogeneous cubic vanishing at all ten is 0. Hence every qᵢ⁽³⁾ = 0, forcing R = 0 — contradicting R(1,0,0) = 1. This corrects an earlier survey that judged Robinson non-SOS to require multi-session Gram-matrix / dual-functional machinery: the elementary zero-set route works because the zeros impose ten independent conditions on the ten-dimensional space of cubic forms.

mainTheorems.name: robinson_not_sos
mainTheorems.description: Robinson's polynomial is not a sum of squares of polynomials: there is no finite family q with R = Σ qᵢ². Discharges the parent axiom robinson_not_sos_aux with 0 axioms.

mainTheorems.name: cubic_zero
mainTheorems.description: The crux: a homogeneous cubic form in three real variables vanishing at the ten real projective zeros of Robinson's polynomial is the zero polynomial. Proved by expanding each evaluation into a linear form in the ten cubic coefficients and clearing the (determinant-128) 10×10 system with linarith.

mainTheorems.name: degree_bound
mainTheorems.description: If Σ qᵢ² = P with totalDegree P ≤ 6, then every qᵢ has total degree ≤ 3 — the no-cancellation property of leading forms of a sum of squares.

mainTheorems.name: topsq
mainTheorems.description: The degree-2D homogeneous component of p² equals the square of the degree-D component when D bounds totalDegree p; gives both the degree bound and the reduction R = Σ (comp₃ qᵢ)².

mainTheorems.name: as_cubic
mainTheorems.description: A homogeneous cubic equals the sum of its ten cubic-monomial terms; turns point evaluation into an explicit linear form in the ten coefficients.
mainTheorems.leanType: q.IsHomogeneous 3 → q = Σ (ten cubic monomials of q)

mainTheorems.name: robinson_isHom
mainTheorems.description: Robinson's polynomial is homogeneous of degree 6, so its degree-6 homogeneous component is itself and off-degree coefficients vanish.

mainTheorems.name: deg3_cases
mainTheorems.description: Every degree-3 exponent vector in three variables is one of the ten cubic monomials — the finite enumeration underpinning as_cubic.

overview: Robinson's polynomial R = x⁶ + y⁶ + z⁶ − x⁴y² − y⁴z² − z⁴x² − x²y⁴ − y²z⁴ − z²x⁴ + 3x²y²z² is, alongside Motzkin's, one of the two classical witnesses that nonnegativity is strictly weaker than being a sum of squares of polynomials — the phenomenon at the heart of Hilbert's 17th problem. The parent gallery entry axiomatized this non-representability (robinson_not_sos_aux); this follow-up proves it from scratch with 0 axioms, reducing the parent's axiom count from 4 to 3. The argument is a zero-set / linear-algebra proof in four moves. First, a degree bound: if R = Σ qᵢ² then each qᵢ has total degree ≤ 3 (the leading forms of a sum of squares cannot cancel). Second, a homogeneous reduction: because R is homogeneous of degree 6, taking degree-6 components gives R = Σ (qᵢ⁽³⁾)² where each qᵢ⁽³⁾ is a homogeneous cubic form — so no separate bottom-degree cascade is needed. Third, vanishing on the zero set: R has exactly ten real projective zeros, (1,±1,0), (1,0,±1), (0,1,±1), (1,±1,±1), and since a sum of real squares is 0 only if each term is, every cubic form qᵢ⁽³⁾ vanishes at all ten. Fourth, the decisive linear algebra: the 10×10 matrix of the ten cubic monomials evaluated at the ten points has determinant 128 ≠ 0, so the only homogeneous cubic vanishing at all ten points is 0; hence every qᵢ⁽³⁾ = 0, forcing R = 0, which contradicts R(1,0,0) = 1. The formalization carries out the last step by expanding each point-evaluation into an explicit linear form in the ten cubic coefficients (as_cubic + eval_mon3) and clearing the resulting determined system with linarith.

conclusion.summary: A 423-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization that Robinson's polynomial is not a sum of squares of polynomials, via the zero-set / linear-algebra route: each cubic form in an SOS decomposition vanishes at R's ten real projective zeros, and the determinant-128 evaluation matrix forces it to be zero. Discharges the parent entry's axiom robinson_not_sos_aux (parent axiom count 4 → 3).
conclusion.implications: Robinson joins Motzkin (sibling hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-02) as a second fully machine-checked example of a PSD polynomial that is not polynomial-SOS — the negative half of Hilbert's 17th problem. Notably, this corrects an earlier project survey that judged Robinson non-SOS to need multi-session Gram-matrix or dual-functional machinery: the elementary zero-set argument succeeds because R's ten zeros impose ten independent conditions on the ten-dimensional space of ternary cubic forms (the evaluation determinant is 128, not 0).
